source.titleEnglish: Talk Through the Mislabeled Gluten-Free Bread
source.objectiveEnglish: Describe a near miss calmly, without blame, and agree with the baker on what will prevent it next time.
source.speakingEnglish: You are Priya's friend, and the AI is Itzel, the baker: calmly explain the misplaced sin gluten sign without blaming her, using por poco, casi and si no hubiera…, podría haber…, then agree with her on one or two steps to prevent it next time.

sourceGrammar.focus: Casi, por poco, podría haber; si clauses (por poco se lo come; si no hubiera leído la etiqueta, podría haber pasado algo)

examples.es: Por poco se come el pan de harina de trigo.
examples.en: She almost ate the wheat-flour bread.

examples.es: Si no hubiera leído la etiqueta, podría haber pasado algo grave.
examples.en: If I hadn't read the label, something serious could have happened.

priorDraft.oldScene: Paris bakery labeling discrepancy and changed shopping decisions
priorDraft.sourceScene: Coyoacán Itzel bakery, misplaced sign and Priya’s uneaten wheat-flour concha

titleFrenchDraft: Expliquer le pain sans gluten mal étiqueté
focusFrenchDraft: Raconter un incident évité de justesse, sans accuser la boulangère, puis convenir de mesures pour éviter une nouvelle confusion.

cards.sourceNoteEnglish: Agrees with the person: Priya es celíaca; a man es celíaco.
Mexican usage; Spain says la bandeja.
Feminine noun that takes el: el área, but separada.
Common in Mexico for one round out of the oven.
Use with present tense for a past near miss: por poco se lo come.

cards.sourceSpanish: Disculpe, Itzel, el letrero de sin gluten está en otra charola.
cards.supportEnglish: Excuse me, Itzel, the gluten-free sign is on another tray.
cards.targetFrenchDraft: Excusez-moi, Itzel, le panneau « sans gluten » se trouve sur un autre plateau.

cards.sourceSpanish: Priya, no te lo comas todavía; espérame tantito.
cards.supportEnglish: Priya, don't eat it yet; wait a sec for me.
cards.targetFrenchDraft: Priya, ne le mange pas encore ; attends-moi un instant.
cards.sourceNoteEnglish: Informal: tú with your friend. Tantito is Mexican for 'a little bit'.

cards.sourceSpanish: Por poco se lo come, pero leí la etiqueta antes.
cards.supportEnglish: She almost ate it, but I read the label first.
cards.targetFrenchDraft: Elle a failli le manger, mais j’ai d’abord lu l’étiquette.

cards.sourceSpanish: Si no lo hubiera visto, podría haberse enfermado.
cards.supportEnglish: If I hadn't seen it, she could have gotten sick.
cards.targetFrenchDraft: Si je ne l’avais pas vu, elle aurait pu tomber malade.

cards.sourceSpanish: No se preocupe, Itzel, nadie tiene la culpa.
cards.supportEnglish: Don't worry, Itzel, nobody is to blame.
cards.targetFrenchDraft: Ne vous inquiétez pas, Itzel, personne n’est en faute.

cards.sourceSpanish: Casi pasa algo, pero lo vimos a tiempo.

cards.targetFrenchDraft: Il a failli se passer quelque chose, mais nous l’avons vu à temps.

cards.sourceSpanish: ¿Qué le parece si usan un código de colores para las charolas?
cards.supportEnglish: What do you think about using a color code for the trays?

cards.sourceSpanish: ¿Podrían dejar el pan sin gluten en un área separada?
cards.supportEnglish: Could you keep the gluten-free bread in a separate area?
cards.targetFrenchDraft: Pourriez-vous garder le pain sans gluten dans une zone séparée ?

reader.sourceSpanish: Un sábado por la mañana, Daniel y su amiga Priya entran a la panadería de Itzel en Coyoacán para desayunar.
reader.supportEnglish: One Saturday morning, Daniel and his friend Priya walk into Itzel's bakery in Coyoacán to have breakfast.
reader.targetFrenchDraft: Un samedi matin, Daniel et son amie Priya entrent dans la boulangerie d’Itzel à Coyoacán pour prendre le petit-déjeuner.

reader.sourceSpanish: Priya es celíaca, así que siempre busca el pan sin gluten antes de pedir.
reader.supportEnglish: Priya is celiac, so she always looks for the gluten-free bread before ordering.
reader.targetFrenchDraft: Priya est atteinte de la maladie cœliaque ; elle cherche donc toujours le pain sans gluten avant de commander.

reader.sourceSpanish: Priya toma una concha de la charola que tiene el letrero de sin gluten.
reader.supportEnglish: Priya takes a concha from the tray that has the gluten-free sign.
reader.targetFrenchDraft: Priya prend une concha sur le plateau qui porte le panneau « sans gluten ».

reader.sourceSpanish: Daniel lee la etiqueta del pan y ve que la lista de ingredientes incluye harina de trigo.
reader.supportEnglish: Daniel reads the bread's label and sees that the ingredient list includes wheat flour.
reader.targetFrenchDraft: Daniel lit l’étiquette du pain et voit que la liste des ingrédients contient de la farine de blé.

reader.sourceSpanish: Daniel: Priya, no te lo comas todavía; espérame tantito.
reader.supportEnglish: Daniel: Priya, don't eat it yet; wait a sec for me.
reader.targetFrenchDraft: Daniel : Priya, ne le mange pas encore ; attends-moi un instant.

reader.sourceSpanish: Daniel: Disculpe, Itzel, el letrero de sin gluten está en otra charola.
reader.supportEnglish: Daniel: Excuse me, Itzel, the gluten-free sign is on another tray.
reader.targetFrenchDraft: Daniel : Excusez-moi, Itzel, le panneau « sans gluten » se trouve sur un autre plateau.

reader.sourceSpanish: Itzel revisa las charolas y se pone roja, porque el pan sin gluten está en la charola de al lado, sin letrero.
reader.supportEnglish: Itzel checks the trays and turns red, because the gluten-free bread is on the tray next to it, without a sign.
reader.targetFrenchDraft: Itzel vérifie les plateaux et rougit : le pain sans gluten est sur le plateau d’à côté, sans panneau.

reader.sourceSpanish: Itzel: ¡Qué pena, fue un descuido mío!
reader.supportEnglish: Itzel: How embarrassing, it was my oversight!
reader.targetFrenchDraft: Itzel : Quelle honte, c’était un oubli de ma part !

reader.sourceSpanish: Daniel: Por poco se lo come, pero leí la etiqueta antes.
reader.supportEnglish: Daniel: She almost ate it, but I read the label first.
reader.targetFrenchDraft: Daniel : Elle a failli le manger, mais j’ai d’abord lu l’étiquette.

reader.sourceSpanish: Daniel: Si no lo hubiera visto, podría haberse enfermado.
reader.supportEnglish: Daniel: If I hadn't seen it, she could have gotten sick.
reader.targetFrenchDraft: Daniel : Si je ne l’avais pas vu, elle aurait pu tomber malade.

reader.sourceSpanish: Daniel explica con calma que, por la celiaquía, Priya no puede comer nada con harina de trigo.
reader.supportEnglish: Daniel calmly explains that, because of celiac disease, Priya can't eat anything with wheat flour.
reader.targetFrenchDraft: Daniel explique calmement qu’en raison de la maladie cœliaque, Priya ne peut rien manger qui contienne de la farine de blé.

reader.sourceSpanish: Daniel: No se preocupe, Itzel, nadie tiene la culpa.
reader.supportEnglish: Daniel: Don't worry, Itzel, nobody is to blame.
reader.targetFrenchDraft: Daniel : Ne vous inquiétez pas, Itzel, personne n’est en faute.

reader.sourceSpanish: Daniel: Casi pasa algo, pero lo vimos a tiempo.
reader.supportEnglish: Daniel: Something almost happened, but we caught it in time.
reader.targetFrenchDraft: Daniel : Il a failli se passer quelque chose, mais nous l’avons vu à temps.

reader.sourceSpanish: Itzel cuenta que la confusión empezó cuando movió las charolas para sacar la horneada nueva.
reader.supportEnglish: Itzel says the mix-up started when she moved the trays to bring out the new batch.
reader.targetFrenchDraft: Itzel raconte que la confusion a commencé quand elle a déplacé les plateaux pour sortir la nouvelle fournée.

reader.sourceSpanish: Itzel: Fue un susto para todos, y necesitamos una medida preventiva para que no se repita.
reader.supportEnglish: Itzel: It was a scare for everyone, and we need a preventive measure so it doesn't happen again.
reader.targetFrenchDraft: Itzel : Cela nous a tous fait peur, et il nous faut une mesure préventive pour que cela ne se reproduise pas.

reader.sourceSpanish: Daniel: ¿Qué le parece si usan un código de colores para las charolas?
reader.supportEnglish: Daniel: What do you think about using a color code for the trays?
reader.targetFrenchDraft: Daniel : Que pensez-vous d’un code couleur pour les plateaux ?

reader.sourceSpanish: Daniel: ¿Podrían dejar el pan sin gluten en un área separada?
reader.supportEnglish: Daniel: Could you keep the gluten-free bread in a separate area?
reader.targetFrenchDraft: Daniel : Pourriez-vous garder le pain sans gluten dans une zone séparée ?

reader.sourceSpanish: Itzel: Me parecen buenas ideas, así que desde mañana las charolas sin gluten van a ser verdes y van a estar en un área separada.
reader.supportEnglish: Itzel: Those sound like good ideas, so starting tomorrow the gluten-free trays will be green and will be in a separate area.
reader.targetFrenchDraft: Itzel : Ce sont de bonnes idées. Dès demain, les plateaux de pain sans gluten seront verts et placés dans une zone séparée.

speakingDraft.roleEnglish: You are Daniel, Priya’s friend, speaking with Itzel at her bakery in Coyoacán after reading the wheat-flour ingredient label. Priya has not eaten the concha.
speakingDraft.openingFrench: Daniel : Excusez-moi, Itzel, le panneau « sans gluten » se trouve sur un autre plateau.
objectivesEnglish: Tell Priya not to eat the concha yet; distinguish the concha’s wheat-flour label from the gluten-free bread on the neighboring unsigned tray.
Explain the near miss and potential illness using faillir and a French counterfactual while preserving that no ingestion occurred.
Explain Priya’s celiac disease directly and calmly without blaming Itzel.
Suggest a color code and separate area, and confirm Itzel’s plan for green gluten-free trays starting tomorrow.
speakingDraft.closureFrench: Daniel : Merci, Itzel. Les plateaux verts et la zone séparée aideront à éviter une nouvelle confusion.

formsDraft.french: Elle a failli manger la concha.
formsDraft.noteEnglish: French a failli + infinitive expresses the near miss; no ingestion is asserted.

formsDraft.french: Si je n’avais pas lu l’étiquette, elle aurait pu tomber malade.
formsDraft.english: If I had not read the label, she could have gotten sick.
formsDraft.noteEnglish: French pluperfect plus conditional past maps the source’s unreal past condition.

formsDraft.french: Priya est atteinte de la maladie cœliaque.
formsDraft.noteEnglish: Keep the clinical diagnosis distinct from a generic food allergy.

formsDraft.french: Le panneau « sans gluten » se trouvait sur le mauvais plateau.
formsDraft.english: The gluten-free sign was on the wrong tray.
formsDraft.noteEnglish: The sign, not the bread’s ingredient label, was misplaced.

formsDraft.french: Dès demain, les plateaux de pain sans gluten seront verts.
formsDraft.english: Starting tomorrow, the gluten-free bread trays will be green.
formsDraft.noteEnglish: Future tense reports Itzel’s agreed preventive step in the source scene.

reviewNotesEnglish: Qualified French and clinical review must check maladie cœliaque and the feminine descriptor for Priya; the source does not diagnose an allergy or say Priya ate the concha.

Keep Itzel’s bakery in Coyoacán, the concha, the wheat-flour ingredient label, the misplaced gluten-free sign, the neighboring unsigned tray and Itzel’s green-tray promise starting tomorrow. The older Paris scene is not a source-equivalent answer.
The source says nobody is to blame while Itzel acknowledges an oversight. Review the French wording for that pragmatic distinction and for formal vous to Itzel versus informal tu to Priya.
A color code and separate area are Itzel’s proposed steps in the scene, not proof that the bread is clinically safe or that cross-contact is eliminated.
